intro: Your P1 is in as you wrote it. "Faithful first" is now a rule: writers keep every point, and the Pangram tool refuses a draft that drops one unless it's only a test. When a faithful version still fails after one more try, it comes to you.

You said "continue", so the rest of Untangling the Belonging Bargains is here, written all at once: P2 and P3, and the h3 Four Pairs That Commonly Hook the Child. Six of its eight new paragraphs pass Pangram alone. Two don't, so they're in as the faithful versions for your fix: Untangling P3 (question 17) and the h3's questions (question 18). Key's credit waits for your word (question 19). The h3, h2 and h1 get checked once those are fixed.

intro: The new h3, the guide's heading. Its last guide paragraph, the credit to Key, is question 19.

rows.article: Pema Chödrön has a quick map
source: Pema Chödrön gives a quick map
notes: All four pairs and all six good things. Writer 1 of two, as written.

rows.label: New, fails Pangram: the questions (question 18)
rows.article: When that happens, you can ask yourself these
source: What do I think I am about to gain or lose?
Whose approval suddenly feels like survival?
Am I protecting a real value, or trying to preserve a high?
What would remain worth doing if nobody praised me for it?
notes: All four questions, reworded. "once you've caught your breath": a reviewer pointed out that asking them at the peak of upset goes against the article's "take a breath or three".
Pangram alone: 100% AI (0.804). In the guide's own words 0.961, and as prose 0.997. In as the faithful version, marked, for your fix.

source: The aim is not to stop enjoying
notes: My rewrite: both writers' drafts failed the linter's coach register.

rows.label: New: differentiation inside
notes: All three comparisons. "It can be the same religion either way" keeps the faith comparison from reading as a verdict on anyone's religion.

rows.label: New: the ordinary-life signs
rows.article: Day to day, differentiation looks something like this
source: In ordinary life, the movement looks like this
notes: As signs ("Noticing…", "Caring…") because "You can…" five times failed the linter. The guide's "love people … without becoming the group identity" is carried by P4 (a reviewer flagged the repeat), so the last sign keeps what's new: questioning while holding the discomfort, without having to stop loving anyone.

rows.label: New: slow and lifelong
rows.article: Differentiation is slow, and it goes on your whole life
notes: The guide's five points. Three rounds of reviews took out tests and reassurances a writer had added (a few visits, the drive home, "you aren't punishing anyone"): each could push a reader toward leaving for good, or back into danger.
